newsitem.title: UK: Littlewoods to buy into Jacques Vert.
newsitem.headline: Littlewoods to buy into Jacques Vert.

text.p: Privately-owned British retailing and leisure giant Littlewoods said on Tuesday that it had sealed a deal with women's fashion group Jacques Vert Plc to bring that company's labelled goods into the home shopping market at the same time as Littlewoods takes a 29.9 percent stake in it.

As part of Jacques Vert's reorganisation and refinancing, also announced on Tuesday, Littlewoods' Home Shopping Group Ltd will subscribe for 9.13 million of the clothing firm's shares at 30p each, for an cost of 2.7 million pounds ($4.48 million), the firms said in a statement.
Littlewoods LWD.CN to buy into Jacques Vert =2
"Today's announcement further strengthens Littlewoods as a major force in the evolution of the home shopping market," the statement quoted Littlewoods chairman James Ross as saying.
"By continuing to meet the demands of today's consumer we will drive our business forward and imporove group profitability," he added.
The first Jacques Vert catalogue, described as being a niche "up-market" entrant should be available in the busy British market in 1998, the firms said.

Last week Littlewoods sealed a 395 million pound buy of the mail order group Freemans from Sears Plc in a key restructuring of the main players in a home shopping market worth an estimated 7.3 billion pounds.

As a result of the Littlewoods' capital injection, plus a further placing and open offer to raise another 3.6 million pounds and new banking facilities, Jacques Vert said it expected to be able to increase its net assets to 6.9 million pounds from 1.3 million while its borrowings would fall to 1.2 million from 7.6 million pounds.
